Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The two umpires make their way out to the middle. Japan Under-19 players are in a huddle, where they are trying to get themselves pumped before they take the field. Will Malajczuk and Nitesh Samuel are the two openers for Australia Under-19. Nikhil Pol to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Australia Under-19 will be pleased with their bowling overall, though conceding 30 extras will be a concern as it pushed the target higher than necessary. William Byrom made an immediate impact on his return, striking with a superb delivery off his very first ball and finishing with two wickets, while Aryan Sharma and Kasey Barton claimed one each. The standout, however, was the leg-spinner, Naden Cooray, who ran through the middle order to take three, and while the chase is manageable, it should still offer the Australian batters a good chance to settle in and gain confidence. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

William Byrom of Australia Under-19 is up for a quick chat. He says that it is a good cricket wicket, and he is happy with the effort of the team. Adds that he loves to put pressure on batters, which either helps him get a wicket or his partner at the other end. Says that he is confident that the batters will chase this down. Ends by saying that he hopes that his domestic team does well in the league, and he goes back to celebrate with them.

Hugo Tani-Kelly then found good support from Charles Hara-Hinze, who played a few attractive strokes during a brief cameo, but his departure triggered a collapse from 105/3 to 118/6. Japan looked in serious trouble at that stage, yet Kelly remained composed, and Montgomery Hara-Hinze chipped in effectively as the two added a crucial 72-run stand. That partnership lifted them closer to 200, with Kelly finishing unbeaten on 79, following up his unbeaten century in the previous game. They would hoped to hit a few more boundaries towards the end, and that is an area of learning for them as they go ahead in their journey.

Despite an early setback, Nihar Parmar and Hugo Tani-Kelly weathered the initial storm well. The runs did not come freely at first, but the pair spent valuable time in the middle and denied Australia further inroads. They put on 58 together before a costly mix-up led to Parmar's dismissal at an inopportune moment.

Full credit to Japan Under-19 for not only batting out the full 50 overs but also pushing their total beyond 200. For a side still finding its feet at this level, that effort will do wonders for their confidence. Australia Under-19 were disciplined for the most part with the ball, though they might feel they missed a chance to finish the job earlier.

A bye to end the innings! William Byrom bowls a good wide yorker, outside off. Chihaya Sekine swings but misses. Hugo Tani-Kelly calls him to steal the run, but he responds late. However, the throw from the keeper goes over the head of the bowler, who is standing in the middle of the pitch. Japan Under-19 finish on 201/8!

However, amidst the rubble, there was a shining gem in opener Hugo Kelly. His unbeaten, resilient century was a masterclass, proving that he has the technique to survive against quality attacks. The challenge for Japan will be finding support for Kelly. Their bowling unit, aside from the spirited Timothy Moore, struggled to contain the flow of runs. To compete here, Japan’s middle order must step up and their bowlers need to find their lengths much quicker than they did against the Sri Lankans. Heading into this clash, Australia start as overwhelming favourites. The disparity in experience and squad depth suggests the Aussies will look to attack from ball one, perhaps eyeing a significant boost to their net run rate. For Japan, this game is about character and small victories, seeing out the new ball and backing up their bowlers in the field. While a Japanese upset would be a miracle, cricket fans will be keen to see if Hugo Kelly can replicate his heroics against one of the best bowling attacks in the competition.
